basis: Mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation uncoupling causes hypermetabolism and characteristic mitochondrial myopathy (Luft disease).
Congenital heart defects and craniofacial skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; short stature alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Glycosylation defect with defining enteropathy and coagulopathy; neurologic abnormalities 80-99%. Renal, hepatic and ocular involvement also qualify but exceed the cap.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the epididymis, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Progressive CNS disease; contractures 5/12 and muscle-fiber abnormalities 3/5 support musculoskeletal damage. Visual impairment lacks proven ocular injury; respiratory failure may be neurogenic.
Severe juvenile arteriosclerosis directly affects arterial walls; no additional organ damage is established.
Tuberculous infection of the urinary bladder; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Intellectual developmental disorder classified as ST3GAL3-related congenital glycosylation disease, establishing neurologic and metabolic axes.
Learning, language and developmental impairment are frequent. Ovarian insufficiency, renal abnormalities and heart defects are occasional; tall stature alone is not skeletal damage.
B-cell lymphoma involving spleen, marrow and blood; lymphoma adds the immune mechanism axis. Associated hepatitis C is a separate disease.
Umbrella vascular disorder defined by inadequate blood supply; no single downstream organ is affected across most subtypes.
Benign or malignant neoplasm originating in or involving skin; other organs are subtype dependent.
Premature ovarian insufficiency is failure of gonadal endocrine function; uterine hypoplasia is outside the axes.
Iodine-related hypothyroidism is a disorder of thyroid hormone production.
Systemic autoinflammation with vasculitis; colitis/oral ulcers 2/2 and hepatic injury 2/2 with cholestasis. Reported arthritis and anemia omitted at cap; transient skin signs excluded.
Viral infection of hematopoietic precursors with characteristic leukopenia and erythrocyte infection. Encephalitis is an uncommon complication despite the parent classification.
Hereditary abnormality of neutrophil morphology; no evidence supplied for immunodeficiency or damage to another organ.
RP2-related retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction, visual-field loss and chorioretinal atrophy.
Structural narrowing of the lacrimal sac; the lacrimal apparatus belongs to the ocular axis.

PREPL-related neuromuscular-junction disease; growth hormone deficiency is a common associated feature, though frequency is unspecified here. Weakness and ptosis do not establish muscle or eye injury.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment in 11/11 patients; no extra-auditory disease established.
Basal cell carcinoma originates in the skin of the external ear, establishing cutaneous and external-ear location; hearing impairment is not inferred.
Leukemia is a hematopoietic malignancy; CNS infiltration is explicitly defining. Leukemia alone does not establish the lymphoma mechanism axis.
Incomplete development of the pituitary endocrine gland; its intracranial location alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Language and neurodevelopmental impairment define the disorder. Hearing impairment and strabismus each occur in 3/12 (25%), below threshold; overlapping eye findings cannot be summed.
